context: Docker build workflow. A teammate wired up an NPM token so the build can fetch private packages, plus registry-based layer caching.
explanation: `build-args` values get baked into the image's build history — `docker history` (or simply pulling and inspecting the pushed image, which is public-readable on many registries) reveals `NPM_TOKEN` in plaintext to anyone. `cache-to: ...,mode=max` makes it worse by also exporting those same layers into the separate cache image. Fix: use a BuildKit secret mount (`--secret id=npm_token,...` in the Dockerfile with `RUN --mount=type=secret`) instead of `build-args` for anything sensitive — secrets mounted this way never persist in a layer.
